transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Occupational health sent me, mostly. They think I’m not eating enough. I don’t know… most days it’s just black coffee, maybe a plain yogurt, or a few bites of chicken at night. Full meals feel like… like I’m letting my standards slip.
What do you mean by 'letting your standards slip' when you think about eating full meals?
I mean… I keep things controlled. Coffee is fine. Maybe a yogurt, maybe a few bites of chicken later. A full meal just feels like too much, like I’m giving in or losing discipline. That’s all.
Are you worried about gaining weight if you eat more than you currently do?
Yeah… I suppose I am. If the scale’s up even half a pound, it hits me. Like I’ve lost control. Then I cut back harder that day. I just… I can’t stand the idea of putting weight back on.
Do you think your weight is currently at a healthy level?

I don’t know. My uniform’s looser, yeah… hangs off me a bit, and I’ve had to tighten my belt past the old notches. But when the nurse said it was dangerously low, I still thought I could be… a little sharper.
Do you think you would be happy with your body if you weighed a bit more

I don’t think so. If I put weight on, I’d just see it here… my stomach, my waist. That’s what I notice in the mirror, not what other people say. If I don’t look lean enough, it… kind of ruins how I feel about myself that day.
Is it more important to you to avoid gaining weight or to achieve a certain body shape?

I guess it’s… both, but the shape is what I see. In the mirror I don’t really see what other people say. I just zero in on my stomach and waist, and if I don’t look lean enough, it’s hard to… respect myself that day.
Do you feel like eating a full meal would make you feel out of control?

Yeah. A full meal feels like… I don’t know, like I’ve let my standards slip. Most days I just keep it small — black coffee, maybe a plain yogurt, or a few bites of chicken at night. Occupational health says I’m not eating enough.
Do you feel anxious when you're eating, like you might not be able to stop?

Not exactly that I won’t be able to stop. It’s more… a full meal makes me feel like I’ve slipped. Like I’m not keeping to what I should. So I keep it small most days — coffee, maybe yogurt, a few bites of chicken later. That’s what occupational health picked up on.
Do you worry that once you start eating a full meal, you won't be able to stop eating?
Not really. I mean… I don’t think it’s that I’d keep eating and couldn’t stop. It’s more just not wanting to have the full meal in the first place.
Do you think you would be able to stop eating once you've started if you were to eat a full meal?
I think I could stop. It’s not really about losing control once I start… it’s more that I don’t want to start with that much food in front of me.
Do you feel like your eating habits are related to a fear of not being able to control yourself around food?
I don’t think so. Not in that way. I’m not really worried I’ll lose control around food… it’s more complicated than that, I suppose.
Is your goal with eating so little to be as thin as possible?

I don’t know if I’d put it that way… “as thin as possible” sounds extreme. I just… when I look at myself, I don’t see what other people say they see. I notice my stomach, my waist. If I don’t look lean enough, it sort of ruins how I feel about myself that day.
Is your main concern with eating more that you will gain weight or that you won't meet your own standards of appearance?

Probably both, but… more the appearance part. If I eat more, I picture it going straight to my stomach or waist. Then I look in the mirror and that’s all I see, and if I don’t look lean enough, it’s hard to feel okay with myself that day.
Is your decision to eat so little mostly because you are afraid of gaining weight?

Yeah… I guess it is. If the scale’s even up half a pound, I get this… jolt, like I’ve messed up or lost control. Then I usually cut back more that day. I just don’t like the idea of putting weight back on.
Is your restrictive eating more about avoiding weight gain or achieving a certain body shape?

More avoiding weight gain, I think. The shape matters, but… if the scale’s up even half a pound, I get that jolt like I’ve lost control. Then I cut back harder because I can’t stand the idea of putting it back on.
Is it the thought of gaining weight that primarily drives your decision to restrict your food intake?
Yeah. Mostly that. If the scale’s up even a little, like half a pound, I feel like I’ve lost control… and then I’ll cut back harder that day. I just don’t want to put weight back on.
Is the fear of gaining weight the main reason you restrict your food intake?
Yeah. I mean… that’s the main thing. If the scale’s up even a little, I feel like I’ve lost control, and I just… cut back harder. I can’t stand the idea of putting weight back on.
Is it the possibility of not meeting your desired body shape that drives you to restrict your food intake more than the fear of gaining weight?

No… not more than the weight. The shape is part of it, I guess, but it’s the scale that gets me. If it’s up even half a pound, I feel like I’ve lost control, and then I cut back harder. I just can’t stand putting weight back on.
Is the fear of gaining weight more important to you than achieving a certain body shape when deciding how much to eat?

Yeah… the weight matters more. If the scale’s up even half a pound, I get this jolt, like I’ve lost control. Then I’ll cut back harder that day. I just… can’t stand the thought of putting weight back on.
